summary:
GlacierWatch is an interactive global web application that leverages Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and multi-mission NASA Earth observation datasets to monitor glacier retreat, track glacial lake expansion, and provide early warnings for Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). Addressing the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, our platform overcomes the critical limitation of optical satellites—which are frequently blinded by persistent mountain cloud cover, heavy monsoon storms, and darkness—by utilizing all-weather, day-and-night SAR backscatter analysis. 

Through a hybrid architecture combining pre-computed high-risk hotspots (such as South Lhonak in India, Imja Tsho in Nepal, and Palcacocha in Peru) with on-demand cloud processing via the Google Earth Engine API, users can analyze any glaciated coordinate worldwide. GlacierWatch fuses SAR water segmentation with NASA topographic and climatic data (NASADEM, GPM IMERG, and GLDAS) to calculate a Universal GLOF Risk Index (0–100%). Featuring a split-screen radar slider, time-series machine learning forecasting, and an interactive "What-If" climate simulator, GlacierWatch turns complex radar signals into actionable, life-saving intelligence for vulnerable mountain communities.
details:
Overview & Problem Statement:

Accelerated climate change is rapidly melting mountain glaciers worldwide, pooling massive volumes of meltwater behind unstable moraine dams. When these natural dams fail, they trigger catastrophic Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), threatening millions of lives and critical infrastructure downstream. Optical satellites often fail to monitor these lakes during peak melting and monsoon seasons due to heavy cloud cover. GlacierWatch solves this by harnessing Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), which penetrates clouds, rain, and darkness to track water expansion continuously.

How It Works (System Architecture):

GlacierWatch operates through a seamless 3-stage workflow:

1. Global Explorer & Hybrid Access:

- Displays global glacier boundaries using NASA NSIDC GLIMS data.

- Provides instant access to Red-Alert Hotspots (5–10 of the world's most dangerous glacial lakes, including South Lhonak, Imja Tsho, and Palcacocha) using pre-computed CSV time series for zero-latency visualization.

- Supports On-Demand Global Analysis, allowing users to click any glacier or input Latitude/Longitude coordinates to trigger real-time cloud processing via the Google Earth Engine (GEE) Python API.

2. SAR & NASA Multi-Sensor Data Engine:

- Applies radar backscatter thresholding (VV/VH polarization in dB) to exploit the specular reflection of calm water, accurately separating expanding glacial lakes from surrounding ice and terrain.

- Features an interactive Split-Screen Map Slider comparing historical vs. recent SAR imagery alongside NASA HLS optical imagery to visually demonstrate radar's superiority during cloudy conditions.

- Integrates terrain slope from NASA NASADEM, precipitation intensity from NASA GPM IMERG, and temperature/snowmelt anomalies from NASA GLDAS.

3. Risk Assessment & Early Warning Dashboard:

- Universal GLOF Risk Index (0–100%): Categorizes risk into Green (Low), Yellow (Moderate), and Red (Critical) based on a weighted multi-factor formula combining SAR lake expansion rate, surrounding terrain slope, extreme rainfall, and temperature anomalies.

- Time-Series Forecasting: Uses Machine Learning (Linear Regression / Prophet) to project future lake surface area expansion based on historical radar trends.

- Interactive "What-If" Simulator: Enables decision-makers and citizens to adjust temperature and rainfall sliders to simulate extreme weather scenarios and observe real-time shifts in flood risk.

Intended Impact & Benefits:

- Early Warning & Disaster Mitigation: Empowers local authorities, hydrologists, and mountain communities with accessible, near-real-time flood risk indicators.

- Science Communication: Bridges the gap between complex microwave remote sensing (SAR backscatter) and public awareness through intuitive visual storytelling.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software:

- Programming Language: Python

- Frontend & UI Framework: Streamlit

- Cloud Geospatial Processing: Google Earth Engine Python API (earthengine-api)

- Interactive Mapping & Visualization: Leafmap, Geemap, Plotly

- Data Science & Forecasting: Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn / Prophet

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

- Hybrid Speed-to-Scale Design: Live cloud processing of SAR imagery can take several seconds; by combining pre-computed CSVs for critical global hotspots with an on-demand GEE engine for custom coordinates, we ensured both instant user experience and limitless global scalability.

- Multi-Sensor Fusion: Moving beyond simple area measurement, our project contextualizes SAR water detection with topographic steepness and hydro-meteorological triggers to assess actual outburst probability.

Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Transparency Acknowledgment:

In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, our team acknowledges the use of Super Intelligence (Large Language Models) to assist in brainstorming system architecture, debugging Python/Streamlit and Google Earth Engine API scripts, and refining project documentation. All SI-assisted code and documentation have been reviewed, tested, and validated by our team, and no NASA branding or logos were generated or modified using SI tools.
